snippet.title: Can AI Compute Become The Next Big Futures Market?
snippet.description:
For decades, companies have turned to futures markets to manage uncertainty. Airlines hedge fuel costs. Farmers hedge crops. Manufacturers hedge metals. Now a startup wants to bring that same financial machinery to artificial intelligence. Silicon Data and CME Group are working on futures contracts tied to GPU rental prices, a market that could help firms hedge rising AI infrastructure, cloud computing and data center costs. AI companies spend heavily to rent high-end GPU power for training and running artificial intelligence models, but future compute prices can be hard to predict.  CNBC's Yun Li reports.

snippet.title: Transcontinental Countries Worldwide 🌍 #Geography #CountryFacts #Europe #Asia
snippet.description:
This video explains how countries qualify as transcontinental under the seven-continents model, distinguishing contiguous states that cross a land border from non-contiguous states with separate territories in another continent. Commonly used continental boundaries include the Ural Mountains and River, the Bosporus, the Sinai land bridge, and the Greater Caucasus watershed. Contiguous examples include Russia across Europe and Asia, Turkey across the Bosporus, Kazakhstan across the Urals, and Egypt via the Sinai. Non-contiguous examples include Denmark with Greenland in North America, France with French Guiana in South America, Spain with the Canary Islands and North African enclaves, and the Netherlands with Caribbean municipalities.

#TranscontinentalCountries #Eurasia #Africa #NorthAmerica #SouthAmerica

snippet.title: What is money? #history #economics #gold #bullion #cash #currency
snippet.description:
Gold is money. Everything else is credit. JP Morgan said it first.

Most people think money is whatever the government says it is. But according to a 1922 article in the Dublin Leader, true money must be a medium of exchange, a unit of account, a store of value, and the basis for future payments. It also needs to be portable, divisible, durable, stable, and easily recognized.

The author concluded that no asset met those requirements better than gold.

A decade earlier, J.P. Morgan said essentially the same thing in just seven words.

Gold's track record is one that can be traced further and further back in history - can we say the same thing about fiat currency?

Newspaper article courtesy of The British Newspaper Archive.
